# Ecclesiastes Chapter 4 -- The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Again I saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And behold, the tears of the oppressed, and they had no one to comfort them! On the side of their oppressors there was power, and there was no one to comfort them.

**2** And I thought the dead who are already dead more fortunate than the living who are still alive. **3** But better than both is he who has not yet been and has not seen the evil deeds that are done under the sun.

**4** Then I saw that all toil and all skill in work come from a man's envy of his neighbor. This also is vapor and a striving after wind.

**5** The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh. **6** Better is a handful of quietness than two hands full of toil and a striving after wind.

**7** Again, I saw vapor under the sun: **8** one person who has no other, either son or brother, yet there is no end to all his toil, and his eyes are never satisfied with riches. "For whom am I toiling and depriving myself of pleasure?" This also is vapor and a grievous task.

**9** Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. **10** For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow. But woe to him who is alone when he falls and has not another to lift him up!

**11** Again, if two lie together, they keep warm, but how can one keep warm alone? **12** And though a man might prevail against one who is alone, two will withstand him — a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

**13** Better was a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knew how to take advice. **14** For he went from prison to the throne, even though he had been born poor in his kingdom. **15** I saw all the living who move about under the sun, along with that youth who was to stand in the king's place. **16** There was no end of all the people, all of whom he led. Yet those who come later will not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vapor and a striving after wind.

---

## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 4 turns from personal experiment to social observation. Qohelet sees three problems: oppression without comfort (vv.1-3), envy-driven competition (v.4), and isolation (vv.7-8). The remedy — or at least the mitigation — is companionship (vv.9-12). The "threefold cord" passage is one of the few genuinely hopeful moments in Ecclesiastes, though even it is followed by the story of the forgotten king (vv.13-16), which shows that even popularity is vapor. The chapter's structure alternates between despair and practical wisdom.

---

## Disagreement Log

## 4:4 — "envy of his neighbor" vs. "rivalry with his neighbor"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-envy [qin'at] of-a-man from-his-neighbor" | Literal — *qin'ah* means jealousy/envy |
| LOGOS | "a man's envy of his neighbor" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "most people are motivated to success because they envy their neighbors" | Expanded paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "a man's envy of his neighbor" (LOGOS). The Hebrew *qin'at ish me-re'ehu* is compact; LOGOS preserves this. PNEUMA's expansion, while insightful, adds interpretive material not in the text.

---

## 4:5 — "eats his own flesh" — literal vs. idiomatic

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "eats his-own-flesh [et-besaro]" | Literal — idiom for self-destruction |
| LOGOS | "eats his own flesh" | Preserves the idiom |
| PNEUMA | "leading them to ruin" | Replaces idiom with meaning |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "eats his own flesh" (EMET/LOGOS). The idiom is vivid and comprehensible in English. PNEUMA's interpretation is correct but loses the imagery.

---

## 4:8 — "vapor and an evil task" vs. "unhappy business" vs. "fleeting and depressing"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "vapor and-an-evil [ra] task [inyan]" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "vanity and an unhappy business" | Formal, softened |
| PNEUMA | "fleeting and depressing" | Dynamic, colloquial |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "vapor and a grievous task." Combines the consensus *hevel* rendering with the weight of *inyan ra* — neither too soft (LOGOS) nor too colloquial (PNEUMA).

---
*-- SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
